docs.title: TreeForge
docs.text:
Turn filesystem directories and AI-generated folder structures into beautiful, customizable diagrams using Mermaid and Graphviz. Smart grouping, depth control, file icons, and multiple export formats.

Generate polished project structure diagrams from a real directory, a list of paths or text produced by an AI.

docs.title: Default appearance
docs.text:
TreeForge uses recognizable file-type icons by default, including folders, images, Office documents, JSON, archives, text, audio and video. The vertical tree without boxes is the default layout.

See the gallery for horizontal layouts, optional boxes, and equivalent diagrams using custom SVG icons.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
python -m pip install .
treeforge render . --max-depth 3 --output tree.svg

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Use TreeConfig in Python or load a JSON/YAML configuration file with --config. YAML uses the optional treeforge[yaml] extra.

{
  "max_depth": 3,
  "max_nodes": 70,
  "min_group": 3,
  "group_by": ["prefix", "extension"],
  "theme": "light",
  "boxes": false,
  "align": "left",
  "colors": {
    "background": "#ffffff",
    "foreground": "#253047",
    "line": "#aabbcc",
    "folder": "#376aab",
    "images": "#a855a0",
    "data": "#d1872c",
    "py": "#438b56"
  }
}

Colors use six-digit hexadecimal values. colors keys may match categories (images, folder, data) or extensions (py, json). Built-in light and dark palettes are available.

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text:
• prefix: only safe numeric sequences with a shared prefix and extension, e.g. frame_001.png, frame_002.png, frame_003.png become frame_*.png.
  • extension: remaining files grouped by logical category (images, documents, data, spreadsheets) or extension.
  • min_group: minimum files needed to create a group.
  • preserve: files to keep visible (README, Dockerfile, etc.).
  • exclude: directory entries to ignore while scanning.
  • max_depth: root is depth 0.
  • max_nodes: total diagram node budget.
  • icons_dir: local directory of user-provided SVG icons for native SVG output in both layouts (see Icons).

Grouping preserves original filenames in each aggregated node's members list.

docs.title: YAML configuration
docs.text: Install YAML support with pip install 'treeforge[yaml]', then use treeforge render . --config treeforge.yaml. YAML files accept the same configuration keys as JSON, using a safe parser.

docs.title: Developer validation suite
docs.text:
The standalone script devtools/run_validation.py is kept outside the installable TreeForge package and is not included in the wheel. It imports the working source via src/ for development only.

python devtools/run_validation.py
python devtools/run_validation.py --output /tmp/treeforge-validation
python devtools/run_validation.py --strict-graphviz

It creates an isolated temporary directory tree and checks equivalence with an AI-style text tree and a path list. It validates grouping, exclusions, depth and node limits, Unicode/CLI, optional Graphviz, SVG icon overrides, rejection of embedded SVG scripts, all native orientation/theme/box/alignment combinations, and TXT/Mermaid/DOT exporters.

It writes validation-output/report.json (machine-readable pass/fail/skip) and validation-output/index.html (visual gallery of generated SVG). Artifacts are intentionally excluded from Git, while the suite is executed by CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Nonzero exit indicates a failed validation. Graphviz is skipped if dot is absent unless --strict-graphviz is passed.

This integration suite complements (rather than replaces) the normal pytest tests.

docs.title: File types and default icons
docs.text:
TreeForge recognizes files by extension and assigns expressive Unicode icons when rendering native SVG, TXT trees or Mermaid node labels.

Family Extensions Icon Microsoft Word and OpenDocument doc, docx, odt 📘 Excel and spreadsheets xls, xlsx, xlsm, ods 📗 PowerPoint and presentations ppt, pptx, odp 📙 Structured data json, jsonl, xml, yaml, yml 🧩 Plain text txt 📃 Markdown md, rst 📝 PDF pdf 📕 Compressed archives zip, tar, gz, 7z, rar 🗜️ Images jpg, jpeg, png, svg, gif, webp, bmp 🖼️ Python py 🐍 Web and code html, css, js, ts, sql 🌐 / 🎨 / 🟨 / 🔷 / 🗄️ Audio mp3, wav 🎵 Video mp4, mov 🎬 Unknown extensions other 📄

Groups of multiple files use their category icon. For custom native SVG icons, add xlsx.svg, json.svg, zip.svg, etc. to an icon directory and pass --icons-dir. Lookup proceeds by extension, category, then general file/folder fallback.

Colors can be configured independently of icons by extension or category using TreeConfig.colors.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: TreeForge requires Python 3.10 or later. It is authored by Sergio Gil-Borrás.

docs.title: Install from the repository
docs.text: python -m pip install .

docs.title: Render a real directory
docs.text:
treeforge render ./project --output tree.svg
treeforge render ./project --layout horizontal --boxes --output horizontal.svg

By default, TreeForge generates a vertical SVG without boxes.

docs.title: Render a text tree
docs.text:
Create a file called structure.txt:

project/
├── src/
│   ├── main.py
│   └── utils.py
└── README.md

treeforge render structure.txt --input-format tree --output structure.svg

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from treeforge import TreeForge, TreeConfig

config = TreeConfig(max_depth=3, boxes=False, theme="light")
tree = TreeForge.from_directory("./project", config)
tree.render("project.svg", layout="vertical")

from_text = TreeForge.from_text("project/\n├── src/\n│   └── app.py\n└── README.md")
from_text.render("diagram.svg")

For path-list input, use TreeForge.from_paths(["src/main.py", "docs/guide.md"]).

See configuration and rendering for other options.

docs.title: Icons and customization
docs.text: TreeForge uses expressive file-type symbols by default, including folder, images, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JSON, ZIP, TXT, music, and video. The default vertical diagram is shown on the home page.

docs.title: Custom SVG directory
docs.text:
Use SVG files named after extensions, categories or general node types:

treeforge render . --icons-dir ./icons --output tree.svg
treeforge render . --icons-dir ./icons --layout horizontal --output horizontal.svg

Python API: TreeConfig(icons_dir="./icons").

For each file, TreeForge checks the extension first (json.svg, xlsx.svg), then the category (images.svg, documents.svg), then folder.svg or file.svg. SVG files must be self-contained and no larger than 64 KiB; embedded scripts and external references are rejected.

Sample icon files are in the repository icons directory.

docs.title: Layouts and rendering
docs.text:
The default is a vertical tree without boxes, using connected SVG paths for branches. Use --layout horizontal for a left-to-right tree; add --boxes for slim node borders with extra spacing.

Layout Output Renderer Vertical (default) SVG Native, connected geometric branches Horizontal SVG Native, orthogonal connectors and left/center alignment Vertical TXT Conventional Unicode tree characters Either MMD Mermaid flowchart source Either DOT Graphviz source Either SVG/PNG/PDF Graphviz with the system dot executable 
treeforge render . --output vertical.svg
treeforge render . --layout vertical --boxes --output vertical-boxes.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --align left --output horizontal.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --align center --boxes --output horizontal-boxes.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --output graph.mmd
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --output graph.dot
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --engine graphviz --output graph.pdf

Boxed native SVG diagrams use smaller, lighter borders and increased node separation. Vertical TXT retains text connectors; native SVG draws them geometrically.

See the generated comparison gallery.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: This page describes proposed future capabilities. Features available in the current development version are documented in the user guides.

docs.title: Visual experience
docs.text:
• Visual regression snapshots and automated geometry comparisons for more complex trees.
  • Additional icon packs and configurable icon-name mapping.
  • Shared theme presets for native SVG, Mermaid and Graphviz.
  • Improved layout measurements for unusually long filenames and Unicode text.

docs.title: Readers and transformation
docs.text:
• Gitignore-aware filesystem scanning.
  • Extended text-tree parsing and more descriptive validation messages.
  • Additional grouping rules, including date patterns and user-supplied matchers.
  • Optional tree comparison and snapshot views.

docs.title: Distribution and integrations
docs.text:
• Interactive HTML explorer with expandable grouped files.
  • Versioned documentation site with stable release-specific URLs.
  • Stable public API and publication to PyPI.

docs.title: Page sizes and diagram readability
docs.text:
TreeForge is primarily a tool for small, curated directory structures. The default vertical SVG assigns each visible node one row. With boxes, rows are taller.

At a nominal CSS rendering scale of 96 pixels per inch:

Vertical layout Row pitch Approximate node rows in 25 cm Plain (default) 34 px = 0.90 cm 27 Boxed 44 px = 1.16 cm 21

These counts are approximate design guidance, not limits enforced by the software. SVG graphics can be resized, but text and icons become harder to read when a large tree is scaled down for an A4 page (29.7 cm high, allowing 25 cm for the diagram after margins). Headers and footers further reduce the available space.

For an A4 document, start with --max-depth 2 and --max-nodes 20, then check the exported diagram. A 30–50-row tree is often better displayed in an online document or broken into smaller diagrams.

Horizontal diagrams depend on leaf count, column width and long names, so there is no useful universal page-size threshold.

The development-only devtools/measure_scale.py prints row-count and physical-size estimates for sample workloads without changing the rendering algorithms.

docs.text:

The four standard filenames always use default icons; the four files ending in -custom.svg use the custom icon directory.

The image files are committed to the repository and can be viewed directly on GitHub or through the documentation website.
